title: Escapements, Regulation, and Timekeeping
description: How a spring's unwind becomes counted ticks, and how those ticks are made honest: lever, balance, hairspring, positions, isochronism.

sourceReferences.title: HSNY Horology 104
sourceReferences.notes: Escapement after the rest of the movement exists. Lever, models, real movements.

sourceReferences.title: WOSTEP Chronometry Adjustments
sourceReferences.notes: Swiss lever adjustments, then regulating organ: poise, hairspring, dynamic poising. Requires a finished simple movement.

modules.title: The escapement
learningObjectives: Release the train in ticks and impulse the oscillator
Name lock, drop, draw, and safety as measured freedoms, not vibes

modules.title: The regulating organ
learningObjectives: Treat period as a property of balance and hairspring, not the train
Contrast a regulator index with a free-sprung balance

modules.title: Timing and positions
learningObjectives: Read daily rate, amplitude, beat error, and positional error on a timing machine
Name temperature, magnetism, and oil as things that move the rate

concepts.name: The escapement
concepts.summary: Turning a spring’s unwind into counted ticks.
objectives: Release the train in ticks and give the oscillator an impulse
State that timekeeping lives in the oscillator period, not in the gears

concepts.name: Recoil versus detached
concepts.summary: Whether the oscillator is left alone between impulses.
objectives: Contrast an oscillator that is dragged between impulses with one left alone
Predict why a detached lever became the modern default

concepts.name: The Swiss lever
concepts.summary: The detached lever as the modern default.
objectives: Describe the Swiss lever as a detached escapement with two pallet stones
Trace lock, impulse, and drop on one beat of the lever

concepts.name: The escape wheel
concepts.summary: The last wheel of the train, delivering impulse.
objectives: Name the escape wheel as the last wheel of the train, delivering impulse
Predict what a bent tooth does to lock and impulse

concepts.name: Pallet stones
concepts.summary: Entry and exit jewels that lock and impulse.
objectives: Give entry and exit jewels the jobs of locking and impulsing
Predict a short lock if a stone is pushed too far in

concepts.name: Impulse and locking
concepts.summary: Two jobs that must not blur.
objectives: Keep impulse and locking as two jobs that must not blur
Diagnose a beat that unlocks without delivering a clean impulse

concepts.name: Draw
concepts.summary: The geometry that pulls the lever onto the banking.
objectives: Use draw to pull the lever onto the banking after impulse
Predict a fluttering lever if draw is missing

concepts.name: Lock, drop, and slide
concepts.summary: The measured freedoms that keep the escapement safe.
objectives: Measure lock, drop, and slide as the freedoms that keep the escapement safe
Predict a rebanking or a stall from the wrong drop

concepts.name: Impulse pin and roller
concepts.summary: How the lever talks to the balance.
objectives: Let the lever talk to the balance through the impulse pin and roller
Predict a missed beat if the pin does not enter the fork horn cleanly

concepts.name: Safety action
concepts.summary: What stops a knock from unlocking the wrong pallet.
objectives: Stop a knock from unlocking the wrong pallet
Name guard pin and safety dart as the geometry that saves the lock

concepts.name: The balance wheel
concepts.summary: The mass that oscillates.
objectives: Treat the balance wheel as the mass that oscillates
Predict how adding or removing inertia changes the period

concepts.name: The hairspring
concepts.summary: The restoring spring that sets the period.
objectives: Treat the hairspring as the restoring spring that sets the period
Predict what a magnetic or concentricity error does to the rate

concepts.name: Regulator versus free-sprung
concepts.summary: Changing effective length versus changing inertia.
objectives: Contrast changing effective length with changing inertia
Predict a drawback of pinning the spring in a regulator boot

concepts.name: What quartz is not doing
concepts.summary: A crystal and a divider, not a lever.
objectives: State that quartz counts a crystal, not a sprung balance
Distinguish a quartz stepper from a mechanical escapement without a luxury claim

concepts.name: Daily rate
concepts.summary: Seconds per day as the number you regulate.
objectives: Read daily rate as seconds gained or lost per day
Predict how a timing-machine trace becomes that number

concepts.name: Isochronism
concepts.summary: Period that does not care about amplitude — in theory.
objectives: Define isochronism as period that does not depend on amplitude
Predict a rate change as the spring winds down if isochronism is poor

concepts.name: Amplitude
concepts.summary: How far the balance swings, and why it fades.
objectives: Measure amplitude as how far the balance swings
Diagnose low amplitude as friction, magnetism, or a tired spring — not as 'it needs a tourbillon'

concepts.name: Positional timing
concepts.summary: Dial up is not pendant up.
objectives: Time the watch in several positions because gravity biases the oscillator
Predict a vertical-position error a pocket watch sees that a wrist already averages

concepts.name: Poising
concepts.summary: A heavy spot on the balance that gravity can find.
objectives: Balance the rim so a heavy spot does not become a positional error
Predict the sign of the rate error when a poise error meets a vertical position

concepts.name: Beat error
concepts.summary: Rest position that is not the middle of the roller.
objectives: Define beat error as unequal time from rest to each unlock
Predict the timing-machine signature of a beat that is out of equal

concepts.name: The timing machine
concepts.summary: A microphone and a diagram of rate, amplitude, beat.
objectives: Read rate, amplitude, and beat error from a microphone trace
Name what the machine cannot see: magnetism, oil placement, a cracked jewel

concepts.name: Temperature and the balance
concepts.summary: Steel that changes modulus when the room does.
objectives: State how temperature changes the modulus and the balance diameter
Predict the compensation a bimetallic or modern alloy is trying to cancel

concepts.name: Magnetism
concepts.summary: A spring that sticks to itself.
objectives: Describe a magnetized hairspring as coils that stick and change the period
Predict the cure: demagnetize, do not 'regulate it out'

concepts.name: Escapement oil
concepts.summary: A tiny film on a pallet stone, and the ways it migrates.
objectives: Oil the impulse faces that need it and keep oil off the lock
Predict a greedy or dry escapement from the wrong drop of oil
